physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Kente cloth, a rectangular woman’s wrapper, composed in white and very dark blue/black cotton, composed of 12 hand-woven narrow strips hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The strips are designed and assembled alternately to form a chequerboard pattern; both ends have five bands with a variant design that serves as a border to the main field. Each narrow strip consists of a ground weave using in the warp white cotton through which run narrow lines of black, and in the weft white cotton alone. A design is introduced in the weft by two blocks of continuous black thread between which are positioned a large variety of geometric patterns created using discontinuous black thread. The warp ends have been left as a fringe.
